items.prompt: Why not compute maximum+1 to build the expected rejection value for signed long long?

options.text: The expected expression itself would overflow
options.why: Validate rejection without executing an undefined expected computation.

options.text: The expected value should use unsigned wraparound and be treated as the signed sum
options.why: An unsigned wrapped value is not a representable signed long long result for maximum+1. The test should verify rejection directly.

options.text: A later cast repairs all earlier undefined operations
Only production arithmetic can have undefined behavior
options.why: Test/harness code follows the same language rules.

items.explanation: A rejection test must not trigger the forbidden operation before reaching the code under test.
